name: deepseek_mcp
summary: DeepSeek OpenAI-compatible inference connector — the cheap-tier rail (~$0.27/M input · $1.10/M output). Three models supported: deepseek-chat (general), deepseek-coder (code generation), deepseek-reasoner (chain-of-thought). Stdlib-only (no `openai` python package). Bearer-auth via studio/auth/keys.upstream_key('deepseek') which resolves DEEPSEEK_API_KEY or INFERENCE_API_KEY. Every successful call appends one InferenceRecord with tier='inference', model='deepseek/<variant>', scope='deepseek_<tool>'.
engine_pattern: ThirdPartyConnector subclass mirroring stripe_mcp shape (Phase A.2). SERVICE='deepseek'. JSON POST to api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions (OpenAI-compat shape). Tool dispatch via send(recipient=tool_name, message=json_args). connect() probes GET /v1/models to verify auth (accepts 200 or 404).

inbound_callers: core/lib/model_api.py (D.1 unified model API — cheap-tier rail)

guarantees: Crystal-anchored — every successful call has a deterministic InferenceRecord with tier='inference', model='deepseek/<variant>'
Stdlib-only — no `openai` package required; uses urllib with application/json POST
Tier-aware — variant model auto-selected via shortcuts (cc deepseek-code routes to deepseek-coder)
Graceful — if no key resolves, connect() returns False and send() emits SendResult(success=False, error='deepseek_not_connected')
Cost-bounded — typical use case (chat + code) is fractions of a penny per call; user's ~$20 lasts months
OpenAI-compatible — same payload shape as hf_hub.inference, swap-able at the router layer
usage_example:
from core.lib.third_party.deepseek_mcp import DeepSeekMCPConnector
c = DeepSeekMCPConnector()
c.connect()
r = c.send('chat_complete', json.dumps({'model':'deepseek-chat','messages':[{'role':'user','content':'hi'}],'max_tokens':50}))
print(r.message_preview, r.crystal_id, r.metadata['tokens_out'])
